tool_input.command:
cd /home/hein/Workspace/Accounting
# Iteratively find and fix companyId mismatches
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  output=$(npx next build 2>&1)
  if echo "$output" | grep -q '✓ Compiled successfully'; then
    echo "BUILD PASSED on iteration $i"
    break
  fi
  
  error_line=$(echo "$output" | grep -B2 'Type error' | head -1)
  error_msg=$(echo "$output" | grep 'Type error' | head -1)
  echo "Iteration $i: $error_line — $error_msg"
  
  # Extract file and line
  file=$(echo "$error_line" | sed 's|^\./||; s|:[0-9]*:[0-9]*$||')
  line_num=$(echo "$error_line" | grep -oP ':\K\d+' | head -1)
  
  if [ -z "$file" ] || [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
    echo "Cannot parse error location, stopping"
    break
  fi
  
  # Read the offending line
  offending=$(sed -n "${line_num}p" "$file")
  echo "  Line: $offending"
  
  # If it's "Expected N arguments, but got N+1" and has companyId, remove companyId arg
  if echo "$error_msg" | grep -q 'Expected.*arguments.*got'; then
    # Remove first arg (companyId) from the function call
    sed -i "${line_num}s/companyId, //" "$file"
    echo "  Fixed: removed companyId arg"
  else
    echo "  Cannot auto-fix, stopping"
    break
  fi
done

-- =====================================================
-- Migration 000: Users, Sessions, and Auth
-- Standalone accounting app authentication tables
-- =====================================================

-- Updated_at trigger function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
  NEW.updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ language 'plpgsql';

-- Users table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id VARCHAR(255) PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::TEXT,
  email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  first_name VARCHAR(255),
  last_name VARCHAR(255),
  role VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'viewer' CHECK (role IN ('super_admin', 'admin', 'manager', 'accountant', 'bookkeeper', 'viewer', 'system')),
  permissions JSONB DEFAULT '[]'::JSONB,
  phone VARCHAR(50),
  department VARCHAR(100),
  profile_picture TEXT,
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  last_login TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_email ON users(email);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_role ON users(role);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_is_active ON users(is_active);

CREATE TRIGGER update_users_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON users
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

-- Covering index for auth queries
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_auth_lookup
ON users(id, is_active)
INCLUDE (email, first_name, last_name, role, permissions, profile_picture, department);

-- User sessions
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_sessions (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token_hash VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
  ip_address VARCHAR(45),
  user_agent TEXT,
  expires_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_sessions_user_id ON user_sessions(user_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_sessions_composite ON user_sessions(id, token_hash, expires_at);

-- User permissions
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_permissions (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  resource VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  action VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  granted BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  granted_by VARCHAR(255) REFERENCES users(id),
  granted_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  CONSTRAINT unique_user_permission UNIQUE (user_id, resource, action)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_permissions_user_id ON user_permissions(user_id);

-- Customers table (standalone, replaces FibreFlow clients reference)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS customers (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255),
  phone VARCHAR(50),
  vat_number VARCHAR(50),
  registration_number VARCHAR(50),
  billing_address TEXT,
  shipping_address TEXT,
  contact_person VARCHAR(255),
  payment_terms INTEGER DEFAULT 30,
  credit_limit NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TRIGGER update_customers_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON customers
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

-- Suppliers table (standalone, replaces FibreFlow suppliers reference)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS suppliers (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255),
  phone VARCHAR(50),
  vat_number VARCHAR(50),
  registration_number VARCHAR(50),
  address TEXT,
  contact_person VARCHAR(255),
  payment_terms INTEGER DEFAULT 30,
  bank_name VARCHAR(100),
  bank_account_number VARCHAR(50),
  bank_branch_code VARCHAR(20),
  bank_account_type VARCHAR(20),
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TRIGGER update_suppliers_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON suppliers
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

-- Customer invoices (standalone, originally from FF migration 149)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS customer_invoices (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  invoice_number VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  customer_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id),
  billing_period_start DATE,
  billing_period_end DATE,
  subtotal NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  tax_rate NUMERIC(5,2) DEFAULT 15.00,
  tax_amount NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
  total_amount NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  amount_paid NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
  status VARCHAR(30) DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN (
    'draft', 'pending_approval', 'approved', 'sent',
    'paid', 'partially_paid', 'overdue', 'cancelled'
  )),
  invoice_date DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,
  due_date DATE,
  sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  paid_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  notes TEXT,
  internal_notes TEXT,
  project_id UUID,
  gl_journal_entry_id UUID,
  created_by VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  approved_by VARCHAR(255),
  approved_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ci_customer ON customer_invoices(customer_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ci_status ON customer_invoices(status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ci_date ON customer_invoices(invoice_date);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS customer_invoice_items (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  invoice_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES customer_invoices(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  quantity NUMERIC(10,2) DEFAULT 1,
  unit_price NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,
  amount NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,
  tax_rate NUMERIC(5,2) DEFAULT 15.00,
  gl_account_id UUID,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TRIGGER update_customer_invoices_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON customer_invoices
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

-- Comments
COMMENT ON TABLE users IS 'Standalone accounting app users';
COMMENT ON TABLE user_sessions IS 'Active user sessions with token hashes';
COMMENT ON TABLE customers IS 'Customer master data for AR';
COMMENT ON TABLE suppliers IS 'Supplier master data for AP';
COMMENT ON TABLE customer_invoices IS 'Customer invoices for AR';

payload.last_assistant_message:
Here's what was wrong and what I fixed:

**Root cause:** `AuthContext` fetches the user from `/api/auth/me` only **once on mount**. After that, the `user` state (including `role` and `permissions`) is stale until a full page refresh or re-login. So when you update someone's role in the DB, the frontend keeps using the old cached values for all `hasRole()`/`hasPermission()` checks.

**The server side is fine** — `getUserAndValidateSession()` reads fresh role/permissions from the DB on every API request. So API-level 403s would work correctly, but the UI wouldn't reflect the change.

**Fix applied:** Added two refresh mechanisms to `AuthContext`:
1. **`focus` event** — re-fetches user when the tab regains focus (immediate pickup when they alt-tab back)
2. **5-minute polling** — fallback to catch changes even if the tab stays active

Now when you change someone's RBAC in the DB, they'll get the updated role/permissions within 5 minutes or as soon as they switch back to the tab.

# Script to auto-fix: find each build error, identify the service function, add _companyId param
# Run build, capture errors, fix each one
cd /home/hein/Workspace/Accounting

for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  ERROR=$(NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 bun run build 2>&1 | grep -A1 "\.ts:" | head -3)
  
  if echo "$ERROR" | grep -q "Compiled successfully"; then
    echo "BUILD PASSED!"
    break
  fi
  
  FILE=$(echo "$ERROR" | head -1 | sed 's/\.\///' | cut -d: -f1)
  LINE=$(echo "$ERROR" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2)
  TYPE_ERR=$(echo "$ERROR" | grep "Type error" | head -1)
  
  if [ -z "$FILE" ] || [ -z "$TYPE_ERR" ]; then
    echo "Could not parse error: $ERROR"
    break
  fi
  
  echo "[$i] $FILE:$LINE — $TYPE_ERR"
  
  # Get the function name being called
  FUNC=$(sed -n "${LINE}p" "$FILE" 2>/dev/null | grep -oP 'await\s+\K\w+|(?<=\s)\K\w+(?=\()' | head -1)
  
  if [ -z "$FUNC" ]; then
    # Try line before
    PREV=$((LINE - 1))
    FUNC=$(sed -n "${PREV}p" "$FILE" 2>/dev/null | grep -oP 'await\s+\K\w+' | head -1)
  fi
  
  echo "  Function: $FUNC"
  
  # Find the function definition
  if [ -n "$FUNC" ]; then
    DEFFILE=$(grep -rn "export.*function $FUNC(" src/modules/ 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    DEFLINE=$(grep -rn "export.*function $FUNC(" src/modules/ 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -d: -f2)
    
    if [ -n "$DEFFILE" ] && [ -n "$DEFLINE" ]; then
      echo "  Definition: $DEFFILE:$DEFLINE"
      
      # Check if it already has _companyId
      if grep -q "_companyId\|companyId" <(sed -n "${DEFLINE}p" "$DEFFILE"); then
        echo "  Already has companyId — skipping (may need different fix)"
        break
      fi
      
      # Add _companyId as first parameter
      sed -i "${DEFLINE}s/function ${FUNC}(/function ${FUNC}(_companyId: string, /" "$DEFFILE"
      echo "  FIXED: Added _companyId param"
    else
      echo "  Could not find definition — manual fix needed"
      break
    fi
  else
    echo "  Could not determine function name — manual fix needed"  
    break
  fi
done

tool_input.prompt:
Fix all TypeScript argument mismatch errors in the ISAFlow app at /home/hein/Workspace/Accounting.

Run `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep "Expected.*arguments"` to see all errors. There are about 78 errors, all of the form "Expected N arguments, but got M".

The root cause: API files were updated to pass `companyId` as the first argument to service functions, but many service function signatures haven't been updated to accept it.

## TWO types of fixes needed:

### Type 1: Service functions called FROM API files with extra companyId
The API files pass `companyId` as the first arg. The service function needs `_companyId: string` added as its first parameter.

Example fix in a service file:
BEFORE: `export async function getFiscalPeriods(): Promise<FiscalPeriod[]> {`
AFTER:  `export async function getFiscalPeriods(_companyId: string): Promise<FiscalPeriod[]> {`

For functions with existing params:
BEFORE: `export async function startReconciliation(bankAccountId: string, ...): Promise<...> {`
AFTER:  `export async function startReconciliation(_companyId: string, bankAccountId: string, ...): Promise<...> {`

### Type 2: Service functions calling OTHER service functions internally
When a service function calls another service function that now has `_companyId` as first param, the internal call also needs updating.

Example: If `completeReconciliation` calls `createJournalEntry(...)` and `createJournalEntry` now expects `_companyId` as first arg, add a placeholder:
BEFORE: `await createJournalEntry({...}, userId)`
AFTER:  `await createJournalEntry('', {...}, userId)`

Or better — pass through the `_companyId` parameter if available.

## Process:
1. Run `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep "Expected.*arguments"` to get all errors
2. For each unique file+function, read the file, fix the function signature or call site
3. After fixing a batch, re-run tsc to check remaining errors  
4. Repeat until zero errors

Fix all TypeScript argument mismatch errors in the ISAFlow app at /home/hein/Workspace/Accounting.

Run `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep "Expected.*arguments"` to see all errors. There are about 78 errors, all of the form "Expected N arguments, but got M".

The root cause: API files were updated to pass `companyId` as the first argument to service functions, but many service function signatures haven't been updated to accept it.

## TWO types of fixes needed:

### Type 1: Service functions called FROM API files with extra companyId
The API files pass `companyId` as the first arg. The service function needs `_companyId: string` added as its first parameter.

Example fix in a service file:
BEFORE: `export async function getFiscalPeriods(): Promise<FiscalPeriod[]> {`
AFTER:  `export async function getFiscalPeriods(_companyId: string): Promise<FiscalPeriod[]> {`

For functions with existing params:
BEFORE: `export async function startReconciliation(bankAccountId: string, ...): Promise<...> {`
AFTER:  `export async function startReconciliation(_companyId: string, bankAccountId: string, ...): Promise<...> {`

### Type 2: Service functions calling OTHER service functions internally
When a service function calls another service function that now has `_companyId` as first param, the internal call also needs updating.

Example: If `completeReconciliation` calls `createJournalEntry(...)` and `createJournalEntry` now expects `_companyId` as first arg, add a placeholder:
BEFORE: `await createJournalEntry({...}, userId)`
AFTER:  `await createJournalEntry('', {...}, userId)`

Or better — pass through the `_companyId` parameter if available.

## Process:

-- Multi-Entity / Multi-Company Support
-- Each company has its own data, users can switch between companies

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS companies (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  trading_name TEXT,
  registration_number TEXT,
  vat_number TEXT,
  tax_number TEXT,
  address_line1 TEXT,
  address_line2 TEXT,
  city TEXT,
  province TEXT,
  postal_code TEXT,
  country TEXT DEFAULT 'South Africa',
  phone TEXT,
  email TEXT,
  website TEXT,
  logo_url TEXT,
  bank_name TEXT,
  bank_account_number TEXT,
  bank_branch_code TEXT,
  bank_account_type TEXT DEFAULT 'current',
  financial_year_start INTEGER DEFAULT 3, -- month (1-12), default March
  vat_period TEXT DEFAULT 'bi-monthly', -- monthly, bi-monthly
  default_currency TEXT DEFAULT 'ZAR',
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS company_users (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id UUID NOT NULL,
  role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user', -- owner, admin, accountant, user, viewer
  is_default BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(company_id, user_id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_company_users_user ON company_users(user_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_company_users_company ON company_users(company_id);

-- Seed a default company
INSERT INTO companies (id, name, trading_name, country)
VALUES ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001', 'My Company', 'My Company', 'South Africa')
ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;

payload.last_assistant_message:
Here's the full picture on multi-company readiness:

## What's in place

| Layer | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **DB schema** | Done | `companies` + `company_users` tables (migration 236), default company seeded |
| **Data scoping** | Done | `company_id` added to all 22 accounting tables, backfilled, NOT NULL, indexes + re-scoped unique constraints (migration 220) |
| **Auto-numbering** | Done | All trigger functions (JE, CP, SP, CN, WO, ADJ, BAT, VA) scope sequences per `company_id` |
| **Backend middleware** | Done | `withCompany()` resolves company from `X-Company-Id` header or user's default |
| **API routes** | Done | All 143 API routes use `withCompany`, passing `companyId` into services (497 references) |
| **Frontend context** | Done | `CompanyProvider` in `_app.tsx`, loads user's companies, persists selection to localStorage |
| **Company switcher UI** | Done | `CompanySwitcher` dropdown in `AppLayout` header — shows all companies, switch + role display |
| **Company settings page** | Done | `/accounting/company-settings` — edit name, VAT, address, banking, fiscal year |
| **`apiFetch` wrapper** | Done | Injects `X-Company-Id` header automatically from localStorage |
| **Company API** | Done | `companyService.ts` — full CRUD, user-company associations, set default |

## One gap: frontend pages use raw `fetch()`, not `apiFetch`

The `apiFetch` wrapper exists and correctly injects the `X-Company-Id` header, but **none of the 104 frontend pages import it**. They all use raw `fetch()`, which means the company header is **never sent** from the UI. The backend middleware will fall back to the user's default company, so it works for single-company use — but **switching companies in the UI won't actually filter data** until pages use `apiFetch`.

This is the only structural gap. Everything else — DB, middleware, services, UI chrome — is wired up and ready. Want me to do a bulk replace of `fetch(` with `apiFetch(` across all the accounting pages?

Thoroughly explore the ISAFlow accounting app at /home/hein/Workspace/Accounting to understand the current multi-company architecture. I need to understand what we have to build on for group/consolidated reporting.

Specifically find and summarize:
1. The `companies` table schema and `company_users` table (in migration SQL files under scripts/migrations/sql/)
2. How `companyService.ts` works (src/modules/accounting/services/)
3. How `withCompany` middleware scopes API requests (src/lib/auth/withCompany.ts)
4. How the financial reporting service works (src/modules/accounting/services/financialReportingService.ts) — what reports does it generate? Does it accept company_id?
5. The trial balance, income statement, balance sheet report services — do they all scope by company_id?
6. Any existing intercompany or cross-company logic
7. The chart of accounts service — is the COA per-company or shared?

Return a detailed summary of the current architecture that's relevant to building group reporting on top of.

-- Multi-Entity / Multi-Company Support
-- Each company has its own data, users can switch between companies

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS companies (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  trading_name TEXT,
  registration_number TEXT,
  vat_number TEXT,
  tax_number TEXT,
  address_line1 TEXT,
  address_line2 TEXT,
  city TEXT,
  province TEXT,
  postal_code TEXT,
  country TEXT DEFAULT 'South Africa',
  phone TEXT,
  email TEXT,
  website TEXT,
  logo_url TEXT,
  bank_name TEXT,
  bank_account_number TEXT,
  bank_branch_code TEXT,
  bank_account_type TEXT DEFAULT 'current',
  financial_year_start INTEGER DEFAULT 3, -- month (1-12), default March
  vat_period TEXT DEFAULT 'bi-monthly', -- monthly, bi-monthly
  default_currency TEXT DEFAULT 'ZAR',
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS company_users (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id UUID NOT NULL,
  role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user', -- owner, admin, accountant, user, viewer
  is_default BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(company_id, user_id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_company_users_user ON company_users(user_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_company_users_company ON company_users(company_id);

-- Seed a default company
INSERT INTO companies (id, name, trading_name, country)
VALUES ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001', 'My Company', 'My Company', 'South Africa')
ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;

-- =====================================================
-- Migration 000: Users, Sessions, and Auth
-- Standalone accounting app authentication tables
-- =====================================================

-- Updated_at trigger function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
  NEW.updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ language 'plpgsql';

-- Users table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id VARCHAR(255) PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::TEXT,
  email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  first_name VARCHAR(255),
  last_name VARCHAR(255),
  role VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'viewer' CHECK (role IN ('super_admin', 'admin', 'manager', 'accountant', 'bookkeeper', 'viewer', 'system')),
  permissions JSONB DEFAULT '[]'::JSONB,
  phone VARCHAR(50),
  department VARCHAR(100),
  profile_picture TEXT,
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  last_login TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_email ON users(email);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_role ON users(role);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_is_active ON users(is_active);

CREATE TRIGGER update_users_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON users
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

-- Covering index for auth queries
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_auth_lookup
ON users(id, is_active)
INCLUDE (email, first_name, last_name, role, permissions, profile_picture, department);

-- User sessions
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_sessions (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token_hash VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
  ip_address VARCHAR(45),
  user_agent TEXT,
  expires_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_sessions_user_id ON user_sessions(user_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_sessions_composite ON user_sessions(id, token_hash, expires_at);

-- User permissions
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_permissions (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  resource VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  action VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  granted BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  granted_by VARCHAR(255) REFERENCES users(id),
  granted_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  CONSTRAINT unique_user_permission UNIQUE (user_id, resource, action)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_permissions_user_id ON user_permissions(user_id);

-- Customers table (standalone, replaces FibreFlow clients reference)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS customers (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255),
  phone VARCHAR(50),
  vat_number VARCHAR(50),
  registration_number VARCHAR(50),
  billing_address TEXT,
  shipping_address TEXT,
  contact_person VARCHAR(255),
  payment_terms INTEGER DEFAULT 30,
  credit_limit NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TRIGGER update_customers_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON customers
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

-- Suppliers table (standalone, replaces FibreFlow suppliers reference)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS suppliers (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255),
  phone VARCHAR(50),
  vat_number VARCHAR(50),
  registration_number VARCHAR(50),
  address TEXT,
  contact_person VARCHAR(255),
  payment_terms INTEGER DEFAULT 30,
  bank_name VARCHAR(100),
  bank_account_number VARCHAR(50),
  bank_branch_code VARCHAR(20),
  bank_account_type VARCHAR(20),
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TRIGGER update_suppliers_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON suppliers
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

-- Customer invoices (standalone, originally from FF migration 149)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS customer_invoices (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  invoice_number VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  customer_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id),
  billing_period_start DATE,
  billing_period_end DATE,
  subtotal NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  tax_rate NUMERIC(5,2) DEFAULT 15.00,
  tax_amount NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
  total_amount NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  amount_paid NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
  status VARCHAR(30) DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN (
    'draft', 'pending_approval', 'approved', 'sent',
    'paid', 'partially_paid', 'overdue', 'cancelled'
  )),
  invoice_date DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,
  due_date DATE,
  sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  paid_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  notes TEXT,
  internal_notes TEXT,
  project_id UUID,
  gl_journal_entry_id UUID,
  created_by VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  approved_by VARCHAR(255),
  approved_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ci_customer ON customer_invoices(customer_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ci_status ON customer_invoices(status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ci_date ON customer_invoices(invoice_date);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS customer_invoice_items (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  invoice_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES customer_invoices(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  quantity NUMERIC(10,2) DEFAULT 1,
  unit_price NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,
  amount NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,
  tax_rate NUMERIC(5,2) DEFAULT 15.00,
  gl_account_id UUID,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TRIGGER update_customer_invoices_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON customer_invoices
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

-- Comments
COMMENT ON TABLE users IS 'Standalone accounting app users';
COMMENT ON TABLE user_sessions IS 'Active user sessions with token hashes';
COMMENT ON TABLE customers IS 'Customer master data for AR';
COMMENT ON TABLE suppliers IS 'Supplier master data for AP';
COMMENT ON TABLE customer_invoices IS 'Customer invoices for AR';

- `bank_name`, `bank_account_number`, `bank_branch_code`, `bank_account_type`

- `vat_period` ('monthly' or 'bi-monthly')

**Default company seeded**: `'00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'` with name "My Company"

---

### 2. **CompanyService.ts Architecture**

Located at `/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/src/modules/accounting/services/companyService.ts`

**Key Functions:**
- `listCompanies()` — returns all active companies
- `getCompany(id)` — fetch single company
- `createCompany(input, userId)` — creates company and auto-assigns creator as 'owner'
- `updateCompany(id, input)` — updates company details
- `getUserCompanies(userId)` — returns list of CompanyUser objects with company name and role (ordered by is_default DESC)
- `setDefaultCompany(userId, companyId)` — sets default company (used in company context resolution)
- `addUserToCompany(companyId, userId, role)` — adds/updates user in company
- `removeUserFromCompany(companyId, userId)` — removes user access

**Usage Pattern**: Services receive `_companyId` parameter (underscore prefix indicates it's currently unused in filtering). The pattern establishes the interface for future multi-company scoping.

---

### 3. **withCompany Middleware** (`src/lib/auth/withCompany.ts`)

**Purpose**: Wraps the `withAuth` middleware to attach company context to request objects.

**Company Resolution Order**:
1. Check `X-Company-Id` request header (set by frontend CompanyContext)
2. Fall back to user's default company (`is_default = true`)
3. Fall back to user's first company by creation date

**What it attaches to request**:
- `companyId` (string UUID)
- `companyRole` (string from company_users.role)

**Authorization**: Validates user has access to requested company via company_users table; returns 403 if not authorized.

**API Response on error**:
- 403: "You do not have access to this company"
- 400: "No company assigned. Please contact an administrator."
- 500: "Failed to resolve company context"

**Used by**: 286+ API endpoints in `/pages/api/accounting/*` (verified via grep)

---

### 4. **Financial Reporting Service** (`src/modules/accounting/services/financialReportingService.ts`)

#### **Income Statement (P&L)**
- Function: `getIncomeStatement(companyId, periodStart, periodEnd, opts, comparePeriod?)`
- **Options available**:
  - `projectId` (optional project filter)
  - `costCentreId` (optional cost centre filter)
- **Output structure**:
  - `periodStart`, `periodEnd`
  - `revenue[]`, `costOfSales[]`, `operatingExpenses[]` (line items with accountCode, accountName, amount)
  - Totals: `totalRevenue`, `totalCostOfSales`, `grossProfit`, `totalOperatingExpenses`, `netProfit`
  - Comparative: `priorTotalRevenue`, `priorGrossProfit`, etc., with variance and variance %
- **Accounts included**: Revenue (account_type='revenue') and Expense (account_type='expense')
- **Date scope**: Filtered by je.entry_date between periodStart and periodEnd

#### **Balance Sheet**
- Function: `getBalanceSheet(companyId, asAtDate, costCentreId?, compareDate?)`
- **Output structure**:
  - `asAtDate` (date)
  - Assets, Liabilities, Equity line items (accountCode, accountName, balance)
  - Totals: `totalAssets`, `totalLiabilities`, `totalEquity`
  - Comparative: `priorTotalAssets`, etc., with variance
  - Calculated field: Retained earnings (current period net profit)
- **Accounts included**: asset, liability, equity types (at level >= 3)
- **Date scope**: All entries where je.entry_date <= asAtDate

#### **VAT201 Return (SA SARS)**
- Function: `getVATReturn(companyId, periodStart, periodEnd)`
- **Output**: VAT201 boxes (output & input) with transaction drill-down
- **Box definitions**: 
  - Output boxes: Boxes 1, 1A, 2, 2A, 3, 12 (by VAT type: standard, capital_goods, zero_rated, export, exempt, reverse_charge, imported)
  - Input boxes: Boxes 14, 15, 14A/15A, 16, 17, 18
- **Details**: Includes transaction-level drill-down with journal entry numbers, dates, descriptions, and amounts
- **Accounts targeted**: Account codes 1140 (Input VAT) and 2120 (Output VAT), plus any account with account_subtype='tax'

#### **Project Profitability**
- Function: `getProjectProfitability(companyId, periodStart, periodEnd)`
- **Output**: Array of per-project profit reports
- **Structure per project**: `projectId`, `projectName`, `revenue`, `costs`, `profit`, `margin%`, `revenueLines[]`, `costLines[]`

---

### 5. **Trial Balance Service** (`journalEntryService.ts`)

- Function: `getTrialBalance(_companyId, fiscalPeriodId, costCentreId?)`
- **Output**: `TrialBalanceRow[]` with accountCode, accountName, accountType, normalBalance, debitBalance, creditBalance
- **Query logic**: 
  - If no cost centre: calls SQL function `get_trial_balance(fiscalPeriodId)`
  - If cost centre: direct query filtered by `jl.cost_center_id = costCentreId`
- **Filter condition**: `je.status = 'posted'` and `je.fiscal_period_id = fiscalPeriodId`

**API Endpoint**: `GET /api/accounting/reports-trial-balance?fiscal_period_id=...&cost_centre_id=...&compare_period_id=...`
- Uses `withCompany` middleware
- Passes `companyId` from request to `getTrialBalance()`

---

### 6. **Income Statement & Balance Sheet Report APIs**

**Income Statement**: `/api/accounting/reports-income-statement`
```
GET ?period_start=YYYY-MM-DD&period_end=YYYY-MM-DD
    &project_id=UUID (optional)
    &cost_centre_id=UUID (optional)
    &compare_start=YYYY-MM-DD (optional)
    &compare_end=YYYY-MM-DD (optional)
```

**Balance Sheet**: `/api/accounting/reports-balance-sheet`
```
GET ?as_at_date=YYYY-MM-DD
    &cost_centre_id=UUID (optional)
    &compare_date=YYYY-MM-DD (optional)
```

**Trial Balance**: `/api/accounting/reports-trial-balance`
```
GET ?fiscal_period_id=UUID
    &cost_centre_id=UUID (optional)
    &compare_period_id=UUID (optional)
```

All use `withCompany` middleware and extract `companyId` from request context.

---

### 7. **Company_Id Scoping Across Data Model** (Migration 220 & 236)

**Tables with `company_id NOT NULL` column**:

**GL Core**:
- `gl_accounts` — per-company COA
- `fiscal_periods` — per-company fiscal calendar
- `gl_journal_entries` — per-company journal entries

**AR**:
- `customers`, `customer_invoices`, `customer_payments`
- `credit_notes`, `customer_write_offs`, `recurring_invoices`

**AP**:
- `suppliers`, `supplier_invoices`, `supplier_payments`
- `supplier_payment_batches`

**Banking**:
- `bank_transactions`, `bank_reconciliations`
- `bank_categorisation_rules`, `categorization_patterns`

**Configuration**:
- `cost_centres` — per-company analysis codes
- `currencies` — per-company currency setup
- `accounting_budgets`, `accounting_adjustments`, `vat_adjustments`
- `recurring_journals`

**Indexing**: All tables have an index on `(company_id)` for performance. Unique constraints have been rewritten to include `company_id`, e.g.:
- `uq_gl_accounts_company_code` on `(company_id, account_code)`
- `uq_customer_invoices_company_number` on `(company_id, invoice_number)`
- `uq_fiscal_periods_company_year_period` on `(company_id, fiscal_year, period_number)`

**Auto-number Functions**: All trigger functions for generating sequential numbers are scoped by `company_id`:
- Journal entries: `JE-YYYY-NNNNN` per company
- Customer payments: `CP-YYYY-NNNNN` per company
- Supplier payments: `SP-YYYY-NNNNN` per company
- Credit notes: `CN-YYYY-NNNNN` per company
- Write-offs, adjustments, batches, VAT adjustments — all scoped per company

**Backfill Pattern**: When migration 220 ran, all existing records were backfilled to the default company `'00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'`, then `company_id` was set to NOT NULL. All existing users were auto-linked to the default company with role='admin' via migration 220.

---

### 8. **Chart of Accounts Service** (`chartOfAccountsService.ts`)

**Per-Company**: Yes, the COA is per-company
- `gl_accounts` table has `company_id NOT NULL` with FK to companies
- Function signature: `getChartOfAccounts(_companyId, includeInactive?)` accepts companyId parameter
- Account codes are unique per company: `UNIQUE(company_id, account_code)`

**Structure**:
- `id`, `account_code`, `account_name`
- `account_type` (asset, liability, equity, revenue, expense)
- `account_subtype` (e.g., 'bank', 'receivable', 'cost_of_sales')
- `parent_account_id` (hierarchical structure)
- `normal_balance` (debit or credit)
- `level` (hierarchy depth)
- `is_active`, `is_system_account`, `description`, `display_order`

**Functions**:
- `getChartOfAccounts(companyId, includeInactive?)` — full COA
- `getAccountTree(companyId, includeInactive?)` — hierarchical tree structure
- `getAccountById(companyId, id)` — single account by ID
- `getAccountByCode(code)` — by account code (NOTE: appears to lack companyId filter in current code)

---

### 9. **Cost Centres / Analysis Codes** (`costCentreService.ts`)

**Per-Company**: Yes
- `cost_centres` table has `company_id NOT NULL`
- Unique constraint: `UNIQUE(company_id, code)`
- Functions accept `_companyId` parameter

**Structure**:
- `id`, `code`, `name`, `description`, `department`
- `cc_type` ('cc1' or 'cc2' for multi-dimensional analysis)
- `is_active`, `created_at`, `updated_at`

**Usage**: Optional filter on journal lines (jl.cost_center_id). Many reports accept `costCentreId` parameter for dimensional filtering.

---

### 10. **Fiscal Periods** (`fiscalPeriodService.ts`)

**Per-Company**: Yes
- `fiscal_periods` table has `company_id NOT NULL`
- Unique constraint: `UNIQUE(company_id, fiscal_year, period_number)`
- Functions accept `_companyId` parameter

**Structure**:
- `id`, `period_name`, `period_number`, `fiscal_year`
- `start_date`, `end_date`
- `status` ('open', 'closing', 'closed', 'locked')
- `closed_by` (user ID), `closed_at`

**Company Configuration**: Each company has its own `financial_year_start` month (stored in companies table), allowing different companies to have different fiscal year calendars.

---

### 11. **Critical Gap: Company_Id NOT Being Filtered in Report Queries**

**ISSUE**: The reporting services (`financialReportingService.ts`, `journalEntryService.ts`) accept `_companyId` parameter but **DO NOT filter queries by company_id**.

**Example from Income Statement**:
```typescript
const rows = (await sql`
  SELECT ga.account_code, ga.account_name, ...
  FROM gl_journal_lines jl
  JOIN gl_journal_entries je ON je.id = jl.journal_entry_id
  JOIN gl_accounts ga ON ga.id = jl.gl_account_id
  WHERE je.status = 'posted'
    AND je.entry_date >= ${periodStart}
    AND je.entry_date <= ${periodEnd}
    AND ga.account_type IN ('revenue', 'expense')
    -- NO AND je.company_id = ${companyId}::UUID
    -- NO AND ga.company_id = ${companyId}::UUID
    ...
`) 
```

**Affected functions**:
- `fetchIncomeStatementRows()` — missing company_id filter
- `fetchBalanceSheetData()` — missing company_id filter
- `getVATReturn()` — missing company_id filter
- `getProjectProfitability()` — missing company_id filter
- `getTrialBalance()` — missing company_id filter in SQL function and cost centre query

**Impact**: In a true multi-company environment with data in multiple companies, reports will return **aggregated data across all companies** instead of company-scoped data.

**Build Requirement**: Before group/consolidated reporting, you must add company_id filters to all reporting query WHERE clauses.

---

### 12. **No Existing Intercompany or Consolidated Logic**

**Findings**: Zero references to:
- `intercompany` (transactions)
- `cross.?company` (cross-company)
- `group.*report` or `consolidated` reporting
- Elimination or netting of intercompany transactions
- Company hierarchy or parent-subsidiary relationships
- Minority interest or ownership percentages

**Current State**: The multi-company architecture is **data-isolation only** (separate data per company). Group/consolidated reporting would be a greenfield feature.

---

### 13. **API Route Architecture**

**Company API**: `/api/accounting/companies`
- `GET` (no params) — returns user's companies
- `GET?action=user-companies` — returns CompanyUser[] with companyId, companyName, role, isDefault
- `GET?id=UUID` — returns company details (with access check)
- `POST` — create new company
- `POST` with `action=set-default` — set user's default company
- `PUT` — update company details (owner/admin only)

**All accounting endpoints** (`/api/accounting/reports-*`, etc.):
- Wrapped with `withCompany` middleware
- Automatically extract `companyId` and `companyRole` from request
- Pass `companyId` to service functions (which currently don't filter)

---

## Summary: What You Have to Build On

**Strengths**:
1. **Solid data isolation foundation**: Every accounting table has `company_id NOT NULL` with proper FK and indexes
2. **Per-company sequential numbering**: Invoice/entry numbers are scoped per company
3. **Company context in all APIs**: `withCompany` middleware ensures every request is company-aware
4. **User-company role model**: RBAC support for owner/admin/accountant/user/viewer roles per company
5. **Dimensional reporting hooks**: Cost centres and projects already baked into journal lines and reports
6. **Fiscal calendar flexibility**: Each company has its own financial_year_start month

**Gaps to Address for Group Reporting**:
1. **Add company_id WHERE clause filters** to all reporting service functions
2. **Design group structure** (parent-subsidiary relationships, ownership %)
3. **Elimination logic** for intercompany transactions
4. **Consolidation rules** (full consolidation, proportionate, equity method)
5. **Group COA mapping** (map company-specific accounts to group accounts)
6. **Multi-currency consolidation** (each company has default_currency field)
7. **Group reporting endpoints** (consolidated P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, etc.)
8. **Audit trail** for consolidation adjustments vs. operating data

**Recommended Starting Point**: Fix the company_id filtering bug first, then build group tables (`company_groups`, `consolidation_mappings`, `consolidation_adjustments`) on top of the working single-company foundation.

- `supplier_payment_batches`

**Banking**:
- `bank_transactions`, `bank_reconciliations`
- `bank_categorisation_rules`, `categorization_patterns`

**Configuration**:
- `cost_centres` — per-company analysis codes
- `currencies` — per-company currency setup
- `accounting_budgets`, `accounting_adjustments`, `vat_adjustments`
- `recurring_journals`

**Indexing**: All tables have an index on `(company_id)` for performance. Unique constraints have been rewritten to include `company_id`, e.g.:
- `uq_gl_accounts_company_code` on `(company_id, account_code)`
- `uq_customer_invoices_company_number` on `(company_id, invoice_number)`
- `uq_fiscal_periods_company_year_period` on `(company_id, fiscal_year, period_number)`

**Auto-number Functions**: All trigger functions for generating sequential numbers are scoped by `company_id`:
- Journal entries: `JE-YYYY-NNNNN` per company
- Customer payments: `CP-YYYY-NNNNN` per company
- Supplier payments: `SP-YYYY-NNNNN` per company
- Credit notes: `CN-YYYY-NNNNN` per company
- Write-offs, adjustments, batches, VAT adjustments — all scoped per company

**Backfill Pattern**: When migration 220 ran, all existing records were backfilled to the default company `'00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'`, then `company_id` was set to NOT NULL. All existing users were auto-linked to the default company with role='admin' via migration 220.

---

### 8. **Chart of Accounts Service** (`chartOfAccountsService.ts`)

**Per-Company**: Yes, the COA is per-company
- `gl_accounts` table has `company_id NOT NULL` with FK to companies
- Function signature: `getChartOfAccounts(_companyId, includeInactive?)` accepts companyId parameter
- Account codes are unique per company: `UNIQUE(company_id, account_code)`

**Structure**:
- `id`, `account_code`, `account_name`
- `account_type` (asset, liability, equity, revenue, expense)
- `account_subtype` (e.g., 'bank', 'receivable', 'cost_of_sales')
- `parent_account_id` (hierarchical structure)
- `normal_balance` (debit or credit)
- `level` (hierarchy depth)
- `is_active`, `is_system_account`, `description`, `display_order`

**Functions**:
- `getChartOfAccounts(companyId, includeInactive?)` — full COA
- `getAccountTree(companyId, includeInactive?)` — hierarchical tree structure
- `getAccountById(companyId, id)` — single account by ID
- `getAccountByCode(code)` — by account code (NOTE: appears to lack companyId filter in current code)

---

### 9. **Cost Centres / Analysis Codes** (`costCentreService.ts`)

**Per-Company**: Yes
- `cost_centres` table has `company_id NOT NULL`
- Unique constraint: `UNIQUE(company_id, code)`
- Functions accept `_companyId` parameter

**Structure**:
- `id`, `code`, `name`, `description`, `department`
- `cc_type` ('cc1' or 'cc2' for multi-dimensional analysis)
- `is_active`, `created_at`, `updated_at`

**Usage**: Optional filter on journal lines (jl.cost_center_id). Many reports accept `costCentreId` parameter for dimensional filtering.

---

### 10. **Fiscal Periods** (`fiscalPeriodService.ts`)

**Per-Company**: Yes
- `fiscal_periods` table has `company_id NOT NULL`
- Unique constraint: `UNIQUE(company_id, fiscal_year, period_number)`
- Functions accept `_companyId` parameter

**Structure**:
- `id`, `period_name`, `period_number`, `fiscal_year`
- `start_date`, `end_date`
- `status` ('open', 'closing', 'closed', 'locked')
- `closed_by` (user ID), `closed_at`

**Company Configuration**: Each company has its own `financial_year_start` month (stored in companies table), allowing different companies to have different fiscal year calendars.

---

### 11. **Critical Gap: Company_Id NOT Being Filtered in Report Queries**

**ISSUE**: The reporting services (`financialReportingService.ts`, `journalEntryService.ts`) accept `_companyId` parameter but **DO NOT filter queries by company_id**.

**Example from Income Statement**:
```typescript
const rows = (await sql`
  SELECT ga.account_code, ga.account_name, ...
  FROM gl_journal_lines jl
  JOIN gl_journal_entries je ON je.id = jl.journal_entry_id
  JOIN gl_accounts ga ON ga.id = jl.gl_account_id
  WHERE je.status = 'posted'
    AND je.entry_date >= ${periodStart}
    AND je.entry_date <= ${periodEnd}
    AND ga.account_type IN ('revenue', 'expense')
    -- NO AND je.company_id = ${companyId}::UUID
    -- NO AND ga.company_id = ${companyId}::UUID
    ...
`) 
```

**Affected functions**:
- `fetchIncomeStatementRows()` — missing company_id filter
- `fetchBalanceSheetData()` — missing company_id filter
- `getVATReturn()` — missing company_id filter
- `getProjectProfitability()` — missing company_id filter
- `getTrialBalance()` — missing company_id filter in SQL function and cost centre query

**Impact**: In a true multi-company environment with data in multiple companies, reports will return **aggregated data across all companies** instead of company-scoped data.

**Build Requirement**: Before group/consolidated reporting, you must add company_id filters to all reporting query WHERE clauses.

---

### 12. **No Existing Intercompany or Consolidated Logic**

**Findings**: Zero references to:
- `intercompany` (transactions)
- `cross.?company` (cross-company)
- `group.*report` or `consolidated` reporting
- Elimination or netting of intercompany transactions
- Company hierarchy or parent-subsidiary relationships
- Minority interest or ownership percentages

**Current State**: The multi-company architecture is **data-isolation only** (separate data per company). Group/consolidated reporting would be a greenfield feature.

---

### 13. **API Route Architecture**

**Company API**: `/api/accounting/companies`
- `GET` (no params) — returns user's companies
- `GET?action=user-companies` — returns CompanyUser[] with companyId, companyName, role, isDefault
- `GET?id=UUID` — returns company details (with access check)
- `POST` — create new company
- `POST` with `action=set-default` — set user's default company
- `PUT` — update company details (owner/admin only)

**All accounting endpoints** (`/api/accounting/reports-*`, etc.):
- Wrapped with `withCompany` middleware
- Automatically extract `companyId` and `companyRole` from request
- Pass `companyId` to service functions (which currently don't filter)

---

## Summary: What You Have to Build On

**Strengths**:
1. **Solid data isolation foundation**: Every accounting table has `company_id NOT NULL` with proper FK and indexes
2. **Per-company sequential numbering**: Invoice/entry numbers are scoped per company
3. **Company context in all APIs**: `withCompany` middleware ensures every request is company-aware
4. **User-company role model**: RBAC support for owner/admin/accountant/user/viewer roles per company
5. **Dimensional reporting hooks**: Cost centres and projects already baked into journal lines and reports
6. **Fiscal calendar flexibility**: Each company has its own financial_year_start month

**Gaps to Address for Group Reporting**:
1. **Add company_id WHERE clause filters** to all reporting service functions
2. **Design group structure** (parent-subsidiary relationships, ownership %)
3. **Elimination logic** for intercompany transactions
4. **Consolidation rules** (full consolidation, proportionate, equity method)
5. **Group COA mapping** (map company-specific accounts to group accounts)
6. **Multi-currency consolidation** (each company has default_currency field)
7. **Group reporting endpoints** (consolidated P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, etc.)
8. **Audit trail** for consolidation adjustments vs. operating data

**Recommended Starting Point**: Fix the company_id filtering bug first, then build group tables (`company_groups`, `consolidation_mappings`, `consolidation_adjustments`) on top of the working single-company foundation.

## IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements: Intercompany Eliminations Summary

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive summary of IFRS 10 requirements for intercompany eliminations:

### Core Requirement

Intercompany eliminations, required under IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements, remove all intra-group balances and transactions before presenting consolidated results. Intra-group assets, liabilities, equity, income, expenses and cash flows are eliminated in full, as are any unrealised profits.

### Scope of Eliminations

IFRS 10 requires eliminating intra-group balances, transactions, income, and expenses in full. This includes sales, purchases, loans, dividends, management fees, and any other intercompany activities.

### Objective and Principle

The objective is simple: show only transactions with external parties. When you eliminate intercompany dealings, your consolidated statements reflect genuine economic activity, not internal shuffling of assets.

### Accounting Policies Uniformity

The parent company should prepare consolidated financial statements using uniform accounting policies. IFRS 10 requires uniform accounting policies across consolidated entities, where practicable.

### Non-Controlling Interests

Upstream eliminations involve subsidiaries selling to the parent company, while downstream eliminations involve the parent selling to subsidiaries. This distinction matters for non-controlling interest calculations, as upstream eliminations affect NCI proportionally, while downstream eliminations typically impact only the controlling interest.

## General Requirements

South African financial reporting is regulated by the Companies Act of 2008 and overseen by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC). Under the Act, all registered entities, including companies and trusts, must prepare annual financial statements—even if they are currently dormant.

## Filing Requirements

An Annual Return is a summary of the most relevant information regarding the company or close corporation and is filed with CIPC while a tax return focuses on taxable income of a company or close corporation in order to determine its tax liability to the State and is filed with SARS. Compliance with the one does not mean that there is compliance with the other. It is two different processes, administered in terms of different legislation by two different government departments.

## Financial Statements Submission

Companies and close corporations, if it is required in terms of Companies Regulation 28 read with Companies Regulation 26 to prepare audited financial statements, must file such with CIPC at the same time of filing its Annual Returns via iXBRL.

## Timeframes

The Companies Act mandates preparation of a business's financial statements within six months of the financial year-end.

## Overview

Intercompany reconciliation is the process of identifying, matching, and eliminating financial transactions between related entities within the same corporate group. These exchanges might include intra-group sales, shared service costs, cross-entity loans, or transfers of cash and inventory.

## Daily Workflow Best Practices

Using a continuous closing approach (also called continuous accounting), where duties typically completed at the end of a fiscal close are done a little bit each day, helps manage intercompany accounting workflow and avoid time crunches at the end of each period. ## Consolidated Trial Balance & Reconciliation

Auto-matching and reconciling intercompany balances across ledgers reduces close-time burdens and implementing real-time data syncing across entities makes reporting faster and more reliable. By reconciling and eliminating intercompany duplicates, you gain clear visibility into the group's net working capital and true control over liquidity.

## Key Challenges

One company's records might not match another's due to timing (e.g., recording a sale in different months), errors, or currency rate differences. This delays reconciliations and can lead to inaccurate financials.

## Automation & Technology Solutions

Platforms like QuickBooks Online Advanced, NetSuite OneWorld, or Oracle Cloud EPM can auto-post intercompany entries, track exceptions, and create consolidated reports with ease. After intercompany transactions are identified, they can be eliminated automatically as part of the consolidation process. Doing this reduces the need for manual intervention and reconciliation.

Based on the web search results, here's the key information about South Africa's Companies Act 2008 regarding group companies, consolidated financial statements, and holding company requirements:

## Definition of Holding Company and Groups

A "group of companies" means a holding company and all of its subsidiaries. A "holding company", in relation to a subsidiary, means a juristic person that controls that subsidiary as a result of any circumstances contemplated in section 2(2)(a) or 3(1)(a).

## Control and Ownership Requirements

In terms of section 3 of the Companies Act, control implies that the holding company, directly or indirectly, owns more than fifty percent of the voting shares (rights) of another company. Any entity that owns more than 50% of the voting shares in another company is considered a holding entity and must compile consolidated financial statements in accordance with International Accounting Standard 27 unless the holding company complies with the exceptions to the reporting standard.

## Consolidated Financial Statement Requirements

The parent (holding) company is obliged to prepare separate as well as consolidated financial statements for the whole group.

## Disclosure Requirements

The following must be disclosed in consolidated financial statements: The extent of restriction of a subsidiary to pay dividends; All significant investments in subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates, as well as the methods by which such investments are accounted for; A schedule indicating the effect of the change in the holding company's interest in the subsidiary that does not give rise to a loss in control by the holding company.

## Key Features for Multi-Entity Accounting Software

### Chart of Accounts Mapping
Financial statement consolidation tools collect financial information from various sources such as ERP systems, spreadsheets, and databases, then map different charts of accounts into a unified structure. Automated mapping tools translate entity-specific account codes to the group chart of accounts, with data validation rules checking for completeness and accuracy during the import process.

### Currency Translation
Without automated systems, consolidation often involves collecting spreadsheets from each entity, manually adjusting for intercompany transactions, converting currencies, calculating minority interests, and producing consolidated reports—a process that can take weeks and often introduces errors. Currency translation happens automatically using appropriate exchange rates for each account type.

### Minority Interest Accounting
When a parent owns more than 50% but not 100% of a subsidiary, the minority share must be isolated and correctly presented on the consolidated balance sheet under ASC 810/IFRS 10. Consolidation tools apply needed adjustments like minority interest calculations and statutory-to-GAAP conversions.

### Consolidation Automation
Multi-entity accounting systems can automate this entire workflow, reducing consolidation from weeks to minutes while improving accuracy. A strong reporting structure incorporates chart of accounts mapping, intercompany eliminations, and entity-specific reporting.

With this feature enabled, NetSuite automatically generates elimination journal entries based on the intercompany transaction lines and intercompany journal lines marked to be eliminated.

NetSuite uses special Elimination Subsidiary records to post elimination journal entries. Elimination transactions post only to the elimination subsidiary and do not affect the general ledger.

## Consolidation Process

At period close, one executes the Eliminate Intercompany task and the system creates elimination journals, which remove intercompany revenues, expenses, receivables, payables, and any unrealized profit/loss from the consolidated results. The Period Close Checklist includes a task to Eliminate Intercompany Transactions, which can only be completed after running the Revalue Open Foreign Currency Balances and Calculate Consolidated Balances tasks.

## Key Benefits

Automated intercompany accounting simplifies reconciliation and elimination of intercompany transactions, saving time and reducing the risk of errors. NetSuite identifies intercompany transactions marked for elimination and automatically generates the necessary journal entries, eliminating artificial profit and loss amounts and ensuring accurate consolidated financial statements.

QuickBooks Enterprise includes multi-company reporting that combines data from multiple company files. Based on the web search results, here's what I found regarding South Africa's SARS group tax relief and Section 45 intra-group transactions under the Income Tax Act:

## Overview

Section 45 of the Income Tax Act allows for the tax neutral transfer of assets between companies forming part of the same group. Section 45 allows companies within the same group to transfer assets without triggering immediate tax consequences such as capital gains tax, income tax, or recoupments.

## Key Requirements

For a transaction to qualify for section 45 relief, several conditions must be met:

- Both the transferor and transferee companies must be South African tax residents, and the companies must form part of the same 'group of companies' as defined in section 41(1) at the end of the day on which the transaction takes place.
- The asset must retain its character in the hands of the transferee, and the consideration for the asset must be appropriate and commercially justifiable.

## Tax Treatment

The transferee company acquires the asset with the same tax cost and characteristics as in the hands of the transferor company, which ensures continuity for tax purposes and prevents any artificial creation or loss of value for tax calculations.

## Anti-Avoidance Provisions

The "de-grouping charge" may apply for up to six years following the conclusion of the intra-group transaction; if the transferor and transferee companies cease to form part of the same group within 6 years, then any deferred tax benefit obtained from the transaction is triggered in the hands of the transferee.

- Each entity files its own IT14 (company tax return) -- no group filing

**Actionable insight:** ISAFlow needs to: (a) track which entities form a "group" per s41 definition, (b) flag intra-group transactions for s45 relief tracking, (c) support per-entity SARS filing plus group consolidated reporting for CIPC, (d) potentially track the 6-year de-grouping window.

---

## 5. Best-in-Class Features (SAP, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks Enterprise)

**Oracle NetSuite OneWorld (gold standard for mid-market):**
- Real-time consolidation across unlimited subsidiaries
- Elimination Subsidiary records -- special entity that holds only elimination journals
- Automated intercompany management: tag POs/SOs as intercompany, system auto-posts elimination JEs on invoicing
- Period Close Checklist with dedicated "Eliminate Intercompany" step
- Multi-book accounting (statutory + management reporting)
- Currency translation with appropriate rates per account type (closing rate for BS, average rate for P&L)
- Subsidiary context switching on all reports
- Daily virtual close capability

**SAP (S/4HANA Group Reporting):**
- Granular control over elimination rules
- Separate Group Reporting module for very large enterprises
- Handles complex ownership structures (partial ownership, cross-holdings)
- Statutory + management consolidation tracks
- More configuration-heavy but extremely flexible

**Sage Intacct:**
- Automated due-to/due-from entries
- Real-time consolidation across entities, currencies, calendars
- Formalized, audit-ready elimination entries
- Dimension-based reporting (can slice by entity, department, project, etc.)

**QuickBooks Enterprise:**
- "Combine Reports from Multiple Companies" feature -- but very limited
- No automatic intercompany eliminations
- No NCI handling
- No currency translation
- Basically just sums balances -- not true consolidation
- Users must finish in Excel

**Feature comparison matrix for ISAFlow to target:**

| Feature | NetSuite | SAP | Intacct | QB Ent | Xero | Target for ISAFlow |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unified CoA mapping | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | No | **Yes** |
| Auto intercompany elimination | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | No | **Yes** |
| NCI / minority interest | Yes | Yes | Partial | No | No | **Phase 2** |
| Currency translation | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | No | **Yes** |
| Real-time consolidation | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | No | **Yes** |
| Elimination subsidiary | Yes | Yes | No | No | No | **Yes** |
| Intercompany transaction tagging | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | No | **Yes** |
| Period close checklist | Yes | Yes | Partial | No | No | **Nice to have** |
| Multi-book (statutory + mgmt) | Yes | Yes | Partial | No | No | **Phase 2** |
| Group dashboard | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | Partial | **Yes** |

---

## 6. Common Accountant Day-to-Day Workflows

**Monthly close workflow:**
1. Each entity completes its own month-end close (bank rec, accruals, prepayments)
2. Intercompany transaction reconciliation -- match Entity A's receivable to Entity B's payable
3. Resolve timing differences (e.g., sale recorded in different months)
4. Generate consolidated Trial Balance with CoA mapping
5. Post elimination journals (intercompany sales/purchases, loans, dividends, management fees)
6. Calculate unrealised profit on intercompany inventory
7. Currency translation for foreign subsidiaries
8. Calculate NCI share of profit/loss
9. Produce consolidated P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow
10. Board pack / management reporting

**Day-to-day needs:**
- **Company switcher**: quickly switch between entities without logging out
- **Group dashboard**: consolidated cash position, AR/AP aging across all entities, combined P&L snapshot
- **Intercompany reconciliation screen**: side-by-side view showing Entity A's intercompany receivable vs Entity B's intercompany payable, with variance highlighting
- **Consolidated Trial Balance**: map each entity's CoA to a group CoA, show entity columns + elimination column + consolidated column
- **Intercompany transaction register**: log of all tagged intercompany transactions with matching status
- **Elimination journal templates**: pre-configured templates for common eliminations (intercompany revenue/expense, loans, dividends)
- **Continuous accounting**: reconcile intercompany throughout the month, not just at close

**Key pain points accountants face:**
- Timing mismatches between entities recording intercompany transactions
- Different charts of accounts across entities requiring manual mapping
- Currency rate differences causing reconciliation breaks
- No single source of truth -- data scattered across spreadsheets
- Manual process takes days and introduces errors
- Audit trail for elimination entries is weak or non-existent

---

This is a goldmine opportunity. Let me synthesize the research into a plan.

---

## Group Company Reporting — Strategic Analysis

### Why this is a killer differentiator

| Competitor | Group/Consolidated Reporting |
|---|---|
| **Xero** | None. 400+ votes requesting it. "Not planned." |
| **Sage 50** | Manual Excel export. Days of work monthly. |
| **QuickBooks Enterprise** | Just sums balances. No eliminations. |
| **Sage Intacct** | Has it — but costs 10x more than Sage 50 |
| **NetSuite OneWorld** | Gold standard — but enterprise pricing |

**The gap**: Mid-market accounting groups (2-15 companies) have zero affordable options with native consolidated reporting. ISAFlow can own this space.

### Critical bug found during research

The report services (`financialReportingService.ts`, `journalEntryService.ts`) accept `companyId` but **don't actually filter by it** in SQL queries. This means reports currently return data from ALL companies mixed together. Must fix before anything else.

---

## Proposed Architecture — 3 Phases

### Phase 1: Foundation (must-have for launch)

**New tables:**
- `company_groups` — defines a group (name, holding company, default currency)
- `company_group_members` — links companies to groups (ownership %, consolidation method, join date)
- `group_coa_mappings` — maps each company's account codes to a unified Group Chart of Accounts
- `intercompany_transactions` — tags and tracks transactions between group entities

**New features:**
- Fix company_id filtering in all report queries (critical bug)
- Group structure setup UI (define parent/subsidiaries, ownership %)
- Group Chart of Accounts with per-company mapping
- Consolidated Trial Balance (entity columns + elimination column + total)
- Intercompany transaction tagging on invoices/payments/journals
- Intercompany reconciliation screen (Entity A receivable vs Entity B payable)
- Group dashboard (combined cash position, AR/AP aging, P&L across entities)

### Phase 2: IFRS 10 Compliance

- Automated elimination journal generation (interco revenue/expenses, balances, dividends)
- Elimination entity (virtual company holding only elimination JEs)
- Non-controlling interest (NCI) calculation
- Unrealised profit elimination on interco inventory
- Multi-currency consolidation (closing rate for BS, average rate for P&L per IAS 21)
- Consolidated Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow
- Goodwill tracking at acquisition

### Phase 3: SA-Specific & Advanced

- Section 45 intra-group transaction tracking with 6-year de-grouping alerts
- Per-entity SARS IT14 + group consolidated AFS for CIPC
- Period close checklist with consolidation steps
- Group budgeting and budget-vs-actual across entities
- Multi-book accounting (statutory vs management)

---

## Proposed Database Schema (Phase 1)

```sql
-- Group definition
CREATE TABLE company_groups (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- "ABC Holdings Group"
  holding_company_id UUID REFERENCES companies(id),
  default_currency TEXT DEFAULT 'ZAR',
  financial_year_start INTEGER DEFAULT 3,
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Group membership
CREATE TABLE company_group_members (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  group_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES company_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  ownership_pct NUMERIC(5,2) DEFAULT 100.00,  -- % held by holding co
  consolidation_method TEXT DEFAULT 'full',     -- full, proportionate, equity
  joined_date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,
  left_date DATE,                               -- for de-grouping tracking
  UNIQUE(group_id, company_id)
);

-- Unified Group COA mapping
CREATE TABLE group_coa_mappings (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  group_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES company_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  group_account_code TEXT NOT NULL,
  group_account_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  group_account_type TEXT NOT NULL,      -- asset, liability, equity, revenue, expense
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  company_account_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES gl_accounts(id),
  UNIQUE(group_id, company_id, company_account_id)
);

-- Intercompany transaction register
CREATE TABLE intercompany_transactions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  group_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES company_groups(id),
  source_company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  target_company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  source_journal_entry_id UUID REFERENCES gl_journal_entries(id),
  target_journal_entry_id UUID REFERENCES gl_journal_entries(id),
  transaction_type TEXT NOT NULL,         -- sale, purchase, loan, dividend, mgmt_fee
  amount NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,
  currency TEXT DEFAULT 'ZAR',
  description TEXT,
  match_status TEXT DEFAULT 'unmatched',  -- unmatched, matched, variance
  variance_amount NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
  transaction_date DATE NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

---

  const ccId = costCentreId ?? null;

export async function getTrialBalance(companyId: string, fiscalPeriodId: string, costCentreId?: string): Promise<TrialBalanceRow[]> {
  try {
    if (!costCentreId) {
      // Use direct query with company_id filter instead of the SQL function
      const rows = (await sql`
        SELECT a.account_code, a.account_name, a.account_type, a.normal_balance,
          COALESCE(b.debit_total, 0) AS debit_balance,
          COALESCE(b.credit_total, 0) AS credit_balance
        FROM gl_accounts a
        LEFT JOIN gl_account_balances b ON b.gl_account_id = a.id AND b.fiscal_period_id = ${fiscalPeriodId}::UUID
        WHERE a.is_active = true
          AND a.company_id = ${companyId}::UUID
          AND (COALESCE(b.debit_total, 0) != 0 OR COALESCE(b.credit_total, 0) != 0)
        ORDER BY a.account_code
      `) as Row[];
      return rows.map(r => ({
        accountCode: String(r.account_code),
        accountName: String(r.account_name),
        accountType: String(r.account_type),
        normalBalance: String(r.normal_balance) as 'debit' | 'credit',
        debitBalance: Number(r.debit_balance),
        creditBalance: Number(r.credit_balance),
      }));
    }

    // Direct query with cost centre filter
    const rows = (await sql`
      SELECT ga.account_code, ga.account_name, ga.account_type, ga.normal_balance,
        COALESCE(SUM(jl.debit), 0) AS total_debit,
        COALESCE(SUM(jl.credit), 0) AS total_credit
      FROM gl_journal_lines jl
      JOIN gl_journal_entries je ON je.id = jl.journal_entry_id
      JOIN gl_accounts ga ON ga.id = jl.gl_account_id
      WHERE je.status = 'posted'
        AND je.company_id = ${companyId}::UUID
        AND je.fiscal_period_id = ${fiscalPeriodId}::UUID
        AND jl.cost_center_id = ${costCentreId}::UUID
      GROUP BY ga.id, ga.account_code, ga.account_name, ga.account_type, ga.normal_balance
      HAVING COALESCE(SUM(jl.debit), 0) != 0 OR COALESCE(SUM(jl.credit), 0) != 0
      ORDER BY ga.account_code
    `) as Row[];

-- ============================================================================
-- 240: Group Company / Consolidated Reporting
-- Enables multi-entity group structures, intercompany tracking,

BEGIN;

-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. Company Groups — defines a holding/subsidiary group
-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS company_groups (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,                              -- "ABC Holdings Group"
  holding_company_id UUID REFERENCES companies(id),
  default_currency TEXT DEFAULT 'ZAR',
  financial_year_start INTEGER DEFAULT 3,          -- month (1-12)
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  created_by UUID,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_company_groups_holding ON company_groups(holding_company_id);

-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. Group Members — links companies to groups with ownership details
-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS company_group_members (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  group_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES company_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  ownership_pct NUMERIC(5,2) DEFAULT 100.00,       -- % held by holding company
  consolidation_method TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'full', -- full, proportionate, equity
  is_holding BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,                  -- true if this is the holding company
  joined_date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,
  left_date DATE,                                    -- for de-grouping tracking (s45 6yr rule)
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(group_id, company_id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_group_members_group ON company_group_members(group_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_group_members_company ON company_group_members(company_id);

-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. Group Chart of Accounts — unified COA for consolidated reporting
-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS group_accounts (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  group_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES company_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  account_code TEXT NOT NULL,
  account_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  account_type TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- asset, liability, equity, revenue, expense
  account_subtype TEXT,                             -- bank, receivable, cost_of_sales, etc.
  parent_account_id UUID REFERENCES group_accounts(id),
  normal_balance TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'debit',     -- debit, credit
  level INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
  display_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(group_id, account_code)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_group_accounts_group ON group_accounts(group_id);

-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 4. COA Mappings — maps each company's accounts to group accounts
-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS group_coa_mappings (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  group_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES company_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  group_account_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES group_accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  company_account_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES gl_accounts(id),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(group_id, company_id, company_account_id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_group_coa_map_group ON group_coa_mappings(group_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_group_coa_map_company ON group_coa_mappings(company_id);

-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 5. Intercompany Transactions — track and reconcile between entities
-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS intercompany_transactions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  group_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES company_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  source_company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  target_company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  source_journal_entry_id UUID REFERENCES gl_journal_entries(id),
  target_journal_entry_id UUID REFERENCES gl_journal_entries(id),
  transaction_type TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- sale, purchase, loan, dividend, mgmt_fee, transfer
  amount NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,
  currency TEXT DEFAULT 'ZAR',
  description TEXT,
  transaction_date DATE NOT NULL,
  match_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unmatched',   -- unmatched, matched, partial, variance
  variance_amount NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
  matched_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  matched_by UUID,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_interco_tx_group ON intercompany_transactions(group_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_interco_tx_source ON intercompany_transactions(source_company_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_interco_tx_target ON intercompany_transactions(target_company_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_interco_tx_status ON intercompany_transactions(match_status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_interco_tx_date ON intercompany_transactions(transaction_date);

-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 6. Consolidation Adjustments — elimination journals for consolidated reports
-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS consolidation_adjustments (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  group_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES company_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  adjustment_number TEXT,                           -- ELIM-YYYY-NNNNN
  adjustment_type TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- interco_revenue, interco_balance, unrealised_profit, nci, currency_translation, goodwill
  description TEXT,
  fiscal_period_id UUID,                            -- period this adjustment applies to
  period_start DATE,
  period_end DATE,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',             -- draft, posted, reversed
  lines JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',                -- [{groupAccountId, debit, credit, description}]
  source_intercompany_id UUID REFERENCES intercompany_transactions(id),
  posted_by UUID,
  posted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_consol_adj_group ON consolidation_adjustments(group_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_consol_adj_period ON consolidation_adjustments(period_start, period_end);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_consol_adj_status ON consolidation_adjustments(status);

-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 7. Auto-number for consolidation adjustments
-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION generate_consolidation_adj_number()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
DECLARE
  adj_year INT;
  next_seq INT;
BEGIN
  IF NEW.adjustment_number IS NOT NULL THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  adj_year := EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(NEW.period_start, CURRENT_DATE));
  SELECT COALESCE(MAX(
    CAST(NULLIF(SPLIT_PART(adjustment_number, '-', 3), '') AS INT)
  ), 0) + 1 INTO next_seq
  FROM consolidation_adjustments
  WHERE group_id = NEW.group_id
    AND adjustment_number LIKE 'ELIM-' || adj_year || '-%';
  NEW.adjustment_number := 'ELIM-' || adj_year || '-' || LPAD(next_seq::TEXT, 5, '0');
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_consol_adj_number ON consolidation_adjustments;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_consol_adj_number
  BEFORE INSERT ON consolidation_adjustments
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION generate_consolidation_adj_number();

-- ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ALTER TABLE gl_journal_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is_intercompany BOOLEAN DEFAULT false;
ALTER TABLE gl_journal_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS intercompany_company_id UUID REFERENCES companies(id);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_je_intercompany ON gl_journal_entries(is_intercompany) WHERE is_intercompany = true;

COMMIT;
